About

I'm a dynamic student leader and digital media professional based in Lagos, currently Co-Founding Nelavista — an AI-powered learning platform working to close Africa's education gap through personalised, affordable tutoring.

My background in mathematics shapes how I approach everything I build: structured, analytical, and grounded in fundamentals. I pair that with hands-on experience in generative AI, prompt engineering, and conversational AI to help brands, schools, churches, and individual creators grow their visibility online.

Outside of building products, I hold executive leadership roles across LASU's Mathematics and Science student bodies, coordinate AI bootcamps for hundreds of students, and mentor upcoming AI creators through my own content and coaching practice.

My Leadership Journey

My Leadership Journey and Achievements

"If you cannot serve, you cannot lead; and if you cannot lead, you cannot truly serve."

— Onovwiome Honourable Onome

My leadership journey has been shaped by a deep commitment to service, innovation, integrity, and meaningful impact. I believe that leadership is not defined by the title one holds, but by the lives one touches, the problems one solves, and the positive change one creates.

As a student leader at Lagos State University (LASU), I have consistently pursued opportunities to strengthen communication, empower students, improve institutional processes, and promote a culture of excellence. My leadership experience has taken me through several positions of responsibility, including serving as General Secretary of the Nigerian Association of Mathematical Science Students (NAMSSN), LASU, a member of the 35th Science Students' Representative Council, and General Secretary-Elect of the Nigerian Association of Science Students (NASS), LASU.

These experiences have provided me with practical exposure to administration, strategic communication, documentation, stakeholder engagement, event coordination, team management, and organizational development. More importantly, they have taught me that effective leadership requires listening before acting, understanding people before making decisions, and taking responsibility when challenges arise.

Beyond traditional leadership structures, I have made digital transformation and innovation a significant part of my leadership philosophy. I have championed the adoption of technology within student communities by introducing innovative digital systems, leveraging artificial intelligence to improve productivity, and advocating for technology-driven solutions to organizational and academic challenges.

Through AI training sessions, mentorship initiatives, and technology-focused programs, I have had the opportunity to equip hundreds of students with practical digital skills that can support their academic pursuits, personal development, and professional careers. These experiences have reinforced my belief that one of the greatest responsibilities of leadership is not simply to lead people today, but to equip others to become better leaders tomorrow.

My commitment to service and excellence has also earned me recognition, including being honoured as Executive of the Year by NAMSSN. Beyond institutional recognition, my leadership experiences have continued to open doors to broader platforms where young leaders are challenged to think beyond their immediate communities and contribute to global development.

My leadership attributes and commitment to social impact have also positioned me to pursue opportunities with renowned international organizations and leadership networks, including the Millennium Fellowship, a global leadership development initiative presented by the United Nations Academic Impact (UNAI) and the Millennium Campus Network (MCN). The fellowship brings together university students from campuses around the world who are committed to advancing the Sustainable Development Goals and creating meaningful social impact within their communities.

Engaging with opportunities of this calibre has expanded my understanding of leadership beyond campus boundaries. It has challenged me to view leadership through a global lens, connect with diverse perspectives, develop solutions to shared challenges, and recognize that meaningful change often begins with individuals who are willing to serve where they are.

My journey has therefore been more than a pursuit of leadership positions. It has been a continuous journey of learning, serving, innovating, empowering, and creating impact. Every position I have occupied has presented a new opportunity to contribute, and every challenge has strengthened my conviction that leadership should leave institutions, communities, and people better than it found them.

As I continue to grow as a leader, my vision is to contribute to building institutions and communities that are more efficient, transparent, inclusive, innovative, and people-centred. I aspire to inspire young people to see leadership not as a privilege of position, but as a responsibility to serve, solve problems, empower others, and create lasting change.

For me, leadership is ultimately about service. It is about choosing responsibility over recognition, impact over applause, and people over position.

"If you cannot serve, you cannot lead; and if you cannot lead, you cannot truly serve."

— Onovwiome Honourable Onome

The World Of Generative AI

Generative AI and My Impact

Generative AI is a branch of artificial intelligence that creates new content such as text, images, videos, audio, and code based on user prompts. It has transformed the way people learn, work, solve problems, and create digital content.

I have embraced Generative AI as a tool for innovation and impact. Through AI, I have trained and mentored students, created educational resources, designed professional graphics and videos, built digital solutions, and helped individuals and organizations improve productivity. By sharing practical AI knowledge and promoting responsible AI adoption, I have empowered others to leverage technology for learning, leadership, creativity, and community development.

The LASU AI Bootcamp (The Eko Revolution), which I hosted, has influenced and empowered over 1,000 students. Beyond the bootcamp, at Nelavista we now have 2,500+ students actively using our AI-powered educational platform, learning and growing with the tools every day.

As AI Lead Consultant for K17 Kapital L.L.C in Dubai, UAE, I work remotely to integrate AI solutions across the company's diversified operations — Oil & Gas, Shipping, Logistics, Dredging, and Aviation — helping streamline decision-making and workflows for an enterprise operating at the intersection of energy, maritime, and strategic mobility across West Africa and beyond.

Speaking has become one of the most direct ways I pass this work on. I was one of the speakers at Google Developers Group (GDG) LASU — Build With AI program, where I taught students and young people how to use AI for content creation and how to apply those same tools across the other parts of their lives: study and revision, personal branding, job and scholarship applications, small business ideas, and everyday productivity. The goal was never to show off what AI can do, but to leave each person in the room with something they could open and use the same evening.

I also served as a distinguished speaker at the Foreign Institute of Research STEM, where I spoke on artificial intelligence in relation to research — how AI can support literature review, data analysis, and hypothesis testing, and more importantly how young researchers can point those capabilities at real problems in their own communities rather than abstract ones. Much of that session focused on framing research questions around issues people actually live with, and using AI to move faster from question to workable solution.

Alongside these, I have spoken at and facilitated a number of other engagements — bootcamps, campus workshops, and mentorship sessions — each built around the same conviction: that AI literacy should not stay locked inside tech circles, and that the fastest way to widen access is to teach it plainly, to as many people as will listen.

THE ERA OF AI UGC CONTENT

User-generated content used to mean a customer's phone-camera review or a creator's honest unboxing video. That's changing fast. Brands, agencies, and everyday creators are now using AI to script, voice, edit, and even "star in" content that looks and feels native to TikTok, Instagram Reels, and YouTube Shorts — product ads, brand stories, explainer videos, and testimonials generated in minutes rather than shot over days with a full production crew.

The numbers show how fast this shift is moving. 92% of brands are already embracing AI-driven UGC, with some seeing engagement rise by as much as 8.7x and cost-per-acquisition drop by roughly 30% as a result. On the broader content side, 87% of marketers now use generative AI in at least one workflow, AI cuts production timelines by up to 80%, and teams using it are publishing 42% more content every month. UGC itself remains the trust engine behind all of it — consumers are 2.4x more likely to see it as authentic than brand-made content, and 80% of Gen Z say UGC videos directly shape their purchase decisions.

What this tells me is simple: the winning approach isn't AI replacing the human voice, it's AI removing the bottleneck between an idea and a finished piece of content — letting one person do the work that used to need a small team, without losing the authenticity that makes people trust what they're watching in the first place. That's the exact space I've been building in — using AI to script, edit, and produce content that still feels personal, native, and worth stopping to watch.

MY AI TOOLS HUB

I don't lean on one tool for everything — I select each one based on the specific problem I'm solving, and I regularly combine several of them within a single project.

I don't rely on one AI tool for everything — I combine them depending on the project. A typical workflow might use ChatGPT or Gemini to develop an idea and write a script, Google AI Studio to prototype the workflow, Nano Banana for visual assets, Google Flow, Veo 3, Kling, or Seedance to turn those assets into video, and ElevenLabs or TTSMaker for the voiceover. This lets me approach AI not just as a chatbot user, but as a creative and technical toolset for building, producing, automating, and solving problems.

AI Generalist Community

Everything I build, teach, and speak about eventually feeds back into one place — a growing community of people who want to actually use AI, not just talk about it. If you've read this far, this is the part where you get to stop reading about the work and start being part of it.

📢 The WhatsApp Channel

My WhatsApp Channel is where I share the fastest-moving updates — the latest tech news, new AI tools and model releases, scholarship and fellowship opportunities, event announcements, and practical AI tips before they show up anywhere else. It's built for people who want to stay sharp and informed without having to dig for it themselves — one follow, and it comes straight to you.

🤝 The AI Generalists Group

Beyond the channel, I run a WhatsApp group for AI Generalists — a committed community of learners figuring out, together, how to use artificial intelligence to create real influence in their communities. It's a space where techies connect, share what they're building, ask questions, exchange opportunities, and hold each other accountable to actually apply what they're learning rather than just consuming content. Whether you're just starting out with AI or already building with it, this is a room full of people moving in the same direction.

Community is where individual effort turns into shared momentum. If you want to stay informed, connect with people doing the same work, and grow alongside a network of AI Generalists — this is your way in.
